summary: Investigated Gizmo's existing two-extension architecture (server-global GizmoServerExtension and session-scoped Pi extensions) and produced a comprehensive design document proposing to unify backends as normal Pi extensions with a small Gizmo bridge for browser-facing descriptors, operations, and events. Includes a four-phase migration plan moving first-party packages (Git, Svelte, Skill authoring, Activity, Unity) from Gizmo server extensions to Pi extensions with versioned frontend host APIs and session-scoped protocol messages.
decisions: Make each backend a normal Pi extension/package rather than a GizmoServerExtension, with a hidden Gizmo bridge used only to publish browser-facing descriptors, operations, events, and optional UI bundle metadata.
Browser extensions should activate only when the corresponding Pi backend is active and must not be required for backend tools, commands, or hooks to function.

Replace project-scoped RPC with session-scoped protocol messages (session.extensions.list, session.extension.invoke, session.extension.subscribe, session.extensions.changed, session.extension.event) with project path as contextual metadata only.
Treat confirmation as a protocol interaction rather than a magic `confirmed` input field on operation inputs.

Bridge communicates via Pi's shared `pi.events` bus with a discovery/register handshake (subscribe to gizmo:register then emit gizmo:discover) so order of bridge vs backend loading does not matter; inject the bridge via DefaultResourceLoader.extensionFactories.
Frontend receives a narrow `GizmoBrowserHost` (sessionId, invoke, subscribe, commands.execute, notifications.show) rather than direct AgentStore/WorkspaceLayout access.
Migrate first-party packages in this order: Git → Svelte → Skill authoring → Activity (move to core UI) → Unity, with GizmoServerExtension kept as a compatibility adapter during Phase 1.

Replace first-extension-wins createView() with composable app-owned declarative slots (inspector tab, command, status item, settings panel, tool-result renderer) and add bundle integrity/version checks with iframe/worker isolation evaluation for third-party UI.
